article.headline: Arm Holdings Holds Buy Range After Heavy-Volume Cup Breakout
article.deck: Arm sits 1.2% above its 299.39 buy point, inside a range that runs to 314.36, with RS rank 94 of 99 on the desk's list.
body: Arm Holdings does not make chips. It designs the processor blueprints that chipmakers, device makers and cloud providers license and build on: CPU designs, graphics and neural-processing accelerators, the interconnects that tie them together, and pre-integrated compute subsystems, along with the software tools to use them. Its revenue comes from licensing that intellectual property and collecting royalties on it.

The quarters show why the stock has led. In the June quarter, EPS rose 108.3% to 0.25 a share and revenue grew 22.4% to $1.29 billion. Over the four quarters listed, EPS moved from 0.22 and 0.21 to 0.29 in the March quarter and 0.25 in June. Revenue climbed from $1.14 billion in the September 2025 quarter to $1.24 billion, then $1.49 billion in March before easing to $1.29 billion in June.

The market pays heavily for that growth. Arm carries a market value of about $323.5 billion, a forward P/E of 98.9 and a trailing P/E of 312.27. Shares are up 177.1% this year and 99.1% over 12 months.

The chart: Arm broke out Sept. 21 from a six-week cup base that ran 24.7% deep, from an Aug. 7 high to a Sept. 3 low. The breakout came on volume 2.66 times the 50-day average. The buy point is 299.39 and the buy range runs to 314.36. Ten sessions later the stock remains inside it.

On Monday Arm fell 1.5%, or 4.59, to 302.9, on volume just 0.55 times average, a quiet pullback. The close sits 1.2% above the buy point. Shares trade 13.6% above the 50-day line at 266.64 and above the 21-day line at 286.8.

The cup formed after a bigger correction. Arm is still 33.1% below its 452.7 peak of June 18 and well up from the 219.39 low of Aug. 3, and the relative strength line sits 33.5% below its high despite the stock's RS rank of 94 of 99 on the desk's list.

The news carries a legal overhang. Qualcomm and Arm began a new trial Monday over chip testing tools, and one report said the two head back to court with billions in potential royalties at stake. Arm also announced the release date for its fiscal second-quarter results; the desk shows Nov. 4.
article.watch: Watch whether Arm holds the 299.39 buy point and the 21-day line at 286.8 through the Qualcomm trial and the Nov. 4 report.
